clue.text: Of which bird-watching is an appropriate example?

definitions.text: Of which bird-watching is an appropriate example?

parts.words: Of which bird-watching is an appropriate example?
parts.note: swap the opening sounds of bird and watching and you get word botching, a fitting description of the very slip of the tongue being asked for

explanation.surface: A question asking what kind of thing the pastime of birding exemplifies.
explanation.walkthrough: The device is named after the Rev William Spooner, famous for swapping initial sounds; bird-watching becomes word-botching, which is exactly what such a slip does.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of transposed-sound slip is a verbal blunder, and the clue's phrase illustrates one while describing it.

clue.text: Two of them overlap slightly in libraries

definitions.text: Two of them overlap slightly in libraries

parts.words: Two of them overlap slightly in libraries
parts.note: the word libraries splits into LIBRA and ARIES sharing one A, two zodiac constellations run together

explanation.surface: A remark about two notices in a library that partly cover each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests notices on a library wall; really the zodiac's Libra and Aries are fused in the word 'libraries', overlapping on their shared A.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra and Aries are both members of the zodiac's twelve, each one of the star symbols astrologers use.

clue.text: Wine expert's drunk one litre, I hope

indicators.note: someone drunk is all over the place, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A wine connoisseur, now tipsy, hopes to have had only a litre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' is the anagram signal, not a description of the expert; the 's after 'expert' simply stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A connoisseur of wines is called by this Greek-derived term meaning lover of wine.

clue.text: Fly endlessly in wild part of Australia

definitions.meaning: the island of Peter Pan, where children fly about and never grow up, a place to fly in for ever
Australians call the remote empty outback of the north by this name

explanation.surface: An insect buzzing without pause in the Australian bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like the insect; it is the verb, recalling Peter Pan's island, while the same name is the Australian term for the remote outback.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is used both for J M Barrie's fantasy island and for Australia's sparsely settled interior.

clue.text: Deliveries paid for with organised amounts of money, say

indicators.note: say tells us to take the spoken form of the phrase before it

parts.note: organised means ran, as in ran a business, and amounts of money are sums

explanation.surface: Goods paid for once the money has been arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells us the phrase is spoken: RAN SUMS (organised, amounts of money) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ransom is the price paid to secure someone's release, a deliverance bought with money.

clue.text: Quarters on top of house in Spanish city

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: S and E, south and east, are two of the compass quarters
a villa is a kind of house

explanation.surface: Lodgings above a house somewhere in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' suggests lodgings, but it means compass points; 'on top of' works because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Spanish spelling of Seville, the Andalusian capital.

clue.text: Top mark secured by champion'

indicators.note: secured by means held inside, so the mark sits within the champion

parts.note: an ace is a champion or expert
M is short for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: The highest score is held by the winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secured by' puts M inside ACE. The page prints 'champion' with no apostrophe; the one in the text is a scanning mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The peak or summit of anything is its highest point.

clue.text: Source of sweet stuff sold in bars

definitions.text: Source of sweet stuff sold in bars

parts.words: Source of sweet stuff sold in bars
parts.note: chocolate, the sweet stuff sold in bars, comes from the beans of this tropical tree

explanation.surface: Something that supplies the sugary products sold in pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' suggests pubs, but these are chocolate bars.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree whose seeds are processed into cocoa and chocolate.

clue.text: Chance of heads getting regular payment?

definitions.meaning: a coin toss gives heads at fifty-fifty, which betting calls these odds
even means regular or steady, so steady pay could be called this, signalled by the question mark

explanation.surface: Asking whether bosses will get a steady salary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' looks like company bosses; it is the side of a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Fifty-fifty betting odds are named this, and read literally it is level, regular pay.

clue.text: Indication of foul play by players — or managers, possibly

definitions.text: Indication of foul play by players — or managers, possibly

parts.words: Indication of foul play by players — or managers, possibly
parts.note: a referee signals a foul by players with a blast of the whistle, and staff expose wrongdoing by managers in the same-named way

explanation.surface: A football match where a foul is spotted, maybe by the coaches.
explanation.walkthrough: The sporting sense is the referee's signal; the second sense is an employee revealing misconduct, here by management.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposing corruption from inside an organisation and a referee's signal share this name.

clue.text: Information part of church got back from Calvinist centre

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: got back says the church part is written backwards

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: Details about a church area returned from the Reformation's headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got back' turns NAVE into EVAN. Calvin led the Reformation from Geneva, so 'Calvinist centre' is that city.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to Geneva, the Swiss city where Calvin preached.

clue.text: Coach, perhaps, that allows player to show full potential

definitions.meaning: a coach, as in a bus, is one example of a means of transport

definitions.text: that allows player to show full potential
definitions.meaning: a showcase role written for an actor to display their talents

explanation.surface: A sports coach who lets a team member reach their best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' and 'player' suggest sport; one is a bus, the other an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a conveyance on wheels and a starring role tailored to one performer go by this word.

clue.text: Most impressive and wise person in top US event

parts.note: superb means magnificent, most impressive
an owl is a byword for a wise person

explanation.surface: A grand, sage figure at America's premier occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: The championship game of American football is the biggest annual US sporting event.

clue.text: Attack far from fair conditions

definitions.meaning: to rush a position and take it by force, as troops do
a tempest is the opposite of fair weather

explanation.surface: An assault launched in very unfavourable circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair conditions' sounds like justice; it is weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent tempest is the reverse of fine weather, and the verb means to assault suddenly.

clue.text: Tolerate the first letters — but I must replace the third

indicators.note: must replace says one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: the first five letters of the alphabet, matching the five-letter answer
the third letter of the alphabet is C

explanation.surface: A grudging instruction to put up with basics while making one swap.
explanation.walkthrough: Start with ABCDE; 'must replace' puts I in place of the third letter, C.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up with something is to bear or endure it.

clue.text: Endured a short time in a strange sort of garden

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places the endured time inside the strange piece

parts.note: rum is British slang for strange or odd
bore means endured, past tense of bear
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Putting up with a brief stay in an odd garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'Endured' looks like the definition's verb but is wordplay, and 'rum' for strange is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical collection of trees is a specialised kind of planted garden.

clue.text: Groom woundingly cut by lover

parts.note: to stab is to cut so as to wound
leman is an old word for a lover or sweetheart

explanation.surface: A bridegroom knifed by his paramour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' reads as a bridegroom; it is a horse groom.
explanation.definitionFit: A groom is someone who looks after horses in a stable.

clue.text: Sound speed isn't wrong for factory worker

parts.note: Mach 1, written MACH I, is the speed of sound

indicators.note: wrong says these letters are set out incorrectly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone denying that their speed is out of line at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' signals the anagram of the apostrophe-free letters of isn't; 'Sound speed' needs the numeral too, as Mach 1 is written with a Roman I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone operating machines in a plant, often sewing machines, is an operative of this kind.

clue.text: One sweetly rewarded for caring for the workers

definitions.text: One sweetly rewarded for caring for the workers

parts.words: One sweetly rewarded for caring for the workers
parts.note: worker bees produce honey, the sweet reward for whoever tends them

explanation.surface: A kindly manager paid back for looking after staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' suggests employees; they are worker bees, and the sweet reward is honey.
explanation.definitionFit: An apiarist keeps hives and harvests the honey the bees make.

clue.text: As usual, overweight after consuming one such pudding

indicators.note: after places the overweight piece behind the usual one

parts.note: par means the normal or usual level

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: fat means overweight
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Being too heavy, as always, after eating a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' is the container signal and 'after' orders the pieces; 'par' for usual comes from golf's standard score.
explanation.definitionFit: A layered frozen dessert or chilled custard dish served in a tall glass.

clue.text: Girl got out of bed for cheese

indicators.note: the girl ends up out of, that is surrounding, the bed so it sits within her letters

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A girl leaves her bed to fetch cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got out of' is the container signal, read as the girl ending up outside the bed on both sides, not as leaving it.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft, mild Italian whey curd is a type of fresh cheese.

clue.text: The weed repeatedly caught in shrub

indicators.note: in says the caught letters go inside the shrub

parts.note: bay is a shrub, the laurel

indicators.note: repeatedly says the letter for caught appears twice

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A weed snagged over and over in a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles the cricket letter and 'in' sets the pair inside the shrub. 'The weed' is jokey slang for tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for tobacco, which is often called the weed.

clue.text: Rise from somewhere below

definitions.meaning: to rise up is to revolt
in the American Civil War a Confederate came from the South, below the Mason-Dixon line

explanation.surface: Coming up from underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below' suggests underground; it is the US South, whose Confederate soldiers were called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolt against authority, and a Confederate soldier from the southern states, share this word.

clue.text: Equipment Jack set up to make colourful cloth

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means written upwards, so the pieces read in reverse

parts.note: kit means equipment
AB, able seaman, is a sailor, as is a jack

explanation.surface: A man named Jack assembling gear to produce bright fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses KITAB as a whole in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesian wax-resist dyed fabric, usually brightly patterned.

clue.text: Counting the cost

definitions.meaning: calculating or working out a total
a bill or settling of accounts, as in the day of judgement

explanation.surface: Weighing up what something will cost.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase; it splits into two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means calculation, and also the bill or settlement one must pay.

clue.text: Miss work for dance

parts.note: a gal is a girl or miss
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Skipping work to go dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a verb; it is a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively nineteenth-century ballroom dance in two-four time.

clue.text: Atlantic liner docked next to a Queen

indicators.note: docked means having its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the Titanic was the liner that sank in the Atlantic

explanation.surface: An ocean liner in port beside a royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' looks like a ship in port; it means cut short, losing the C.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's queen of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Unimportant whether it's four or six in test

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the test

parts.note: a trial is a test
IV is four in Roman numerals; VI, six, works too since TR+VI+IAL gives the same word

explanation.surface: It hardly matters which boundary a batsman hits in a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'in' as the container signal, either numeral works: VI placed one letter later inside the test gives the same answer, hence 'whether it's'. The surface suggests cricket boundaries in a Test match.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of little significance or consequence.

clue.text: Fashion model

definitions.meaning: a brand or type of product, as of a car

explanation.surface: Someone who models clothes on a catwalk.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase looks like a catwalk model; it is two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to create, and the noun names a brand or type of car.

clue.text: Sound of a lost sheep? Honestly!

indicators.note: sound of says we want what the phrase is like when spoken

parts.note: a lost animal is a stray, and a tup is a ram

explanation.surface: An exclamation of disbelief about the noise a missing sheep makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound of' looks like bleating; it means the spoken form. STRAY TUP is said like the answer; a tup is a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is slang meaning truthfully or without exaggeration.
